Purpose of Road Safety Audit A Road Safety Audit (RSA) is a formal examination of an existing or future road project to determine its potential to cause road accidents or casualties. The audit independently evaluates road safety performance using a defined checklist methodology. 2. Black Spot Identification Method (IRC) IRC recommends the following quantitative method for black spot identification: Accident Frequency Method: Sections with 5+ injury accidents in 3 years qualify as black spots. Accident Rate Method: Accident rate per vehicle kilometer traveled (VKT) above threshold triggers black spot classification. Severity Index: Weighted score = (12 × Fatal + 3 × Grievous + 1 × Simple) / Total accidents. Sites scoring 15 are high priority. 3. Transition curves at sharp bends. Adequate shoulder width (minimum 2.5m on 2 lane highways). 3.2 Road Furniture Chevron signs at curves exceeding 30° deflection. Delineators at 10m spacing in curves. W beam guardrails on embankments 3m height. 3.3 Junctions Priority control signs at all intersections. Channelization islands for turning movements. Maharashtra has identified over 450 black spots on state and national highways within the state as of 2022. 2.
